page8.explanatoryAddition: Returns blood from the upper body to the right atrium.
Returns blood from the lower body to the right atrium.
Receives systemic venous blood before the tricuspid valve.
Separates right atrium and right ventricle; limits backward flow during ventricular contraction.
Pumps blood through its outflow region and pulmonary valve toward the lungs.
The right ventricular outflow region below the pulmonary valve; not a separate chamber.
Semilunar valve between the right ventricular outflow and pulmonary trunk.
The common vessel leaving the right ventricle before it branches toward the lungs.
Carries blood toward the left lung; oxygen-poor in normal adult circulation.
page8.status: Lesson representation; direct mock assessment gap

page8.explanatoryAddition: Return oxygen-rich blood from the left lung to the left atrium.
Receives pulmonary venous blood before the mitral valve.
The left AV/bicuspid valve between the left atrium and ventricle.
Pumps into the aorta and has the thick systemic-pumping muscle wall.
Semilunar valve between left ventricle and aorta.
The initial upward part of the aorta after the aortic valve.
The curved continuation of the ascending aorta.
Separates the right and left atria.
Separates the right and left ventricles.
Ventricular muscle that tensions the chordae tendineae.
Cords between AV valve cusps and papillary muscles; not semilunar valve supports.
Muscular ridges on the inner ventricular walls.
